content.value_statement: Manual data cleanup can consume many tokens and introduce inconsistent results. This skill gives Claude, Codex, and Claude Code reusable JavaScript patterns for filtering, mapping, sorting, aggregating, and deduplicating records.
actual_capabilities: Filters records with custom predicate functions.
Maps records into normalized objects with custom functions.
Sorts records by one field in ascending or descending order.
Computes sum, average, count, minimum, and maximum for one field.
Removes duplicate records by one field value.
Shows examples for MCP database query and storage workflows.
limitations: The skill documents JavaScript examples but does not include a separate runnable package file.
Callbacks must be written by the user or agent, so untrusted logic should not run.
It handles arrays of objects, not streaming or distributed datasets.
Aggregations are simple and operate on one field at a time.

use_cases.title: Clean Customer Exports
use_cases.description: A data analyst can trim fields, normalize emails, and remove duplicate customer records before reporting.

use_cases.title: Summarize Sales Records
use_cases.description: An operations manager can filter completed orders, sort by value, and calculate total or average revenue.

use_cases.title: Prepare MCP Query Results
use_cases.description: A developer can process database tool results before saving a concise summary for an agent workflow.

prompt_templates.title: Filter a List
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the data-processor skill to keep only completed sales records. Sort the remaining records by amount from highest to lowest.

prompt_templates.title: Normalize Records
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the data-processor skill to trim customer names, lowercase email addresses, remove duplicate emails, and summarize the changes.

prompt_templates.title: Aggregate Results
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the data-processor skill to filter active accounts and calculate the total revenue field. Return only the key summary.

prompt_templates.title: Process MCP Data
prompt_templates.prompt: Query customer records with the available MCP tool, process active accounts with this skill, save the processed records, and return summary statistics.

output_examples.input: A sales list contains completed and pending orders with amount values.
output_examples.output: Returns only completed orders, sorted by amount, with a short count of removed records.

output_examples.input: A customer export contains repeated email addresses and inconsistent capitalization.
output_examples.output: Returns normalized customer records, removes duplicate emails, and reports how many records remain.

output_examples.input: A list of orders needs a total for one numeric field.
output_examples.output: Returns the original records with a summary showing the selected field and calculated total.

best_practices: Validate input arrays before processing them.
Return concise statistics to the agent instead of full large datasets.
Save intermediate results when processing large records across several steps.
anti_patterns: Do not run callback logic from untrusted users.
Do not send full sensitive datasets back to the model when a summary is enough.
Do not use this skill for streaming jobs or very large distributed data.

faq.question: What type of data does this skill process?
faq.answer: It processes arrays of object records, such as sales rows, customer exports, and query results.

faq.question: Does it include a ready package file?
faq.answer: No. The skill provides reusable JavaScript examples inside SKILL.md.

faq.question: Can Claude, Codex, and Claude Code use it?
faq.answer: Yes. The report declares support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.

faq.question: Can it aggregate data?
faq.answer: Yes. It demonstrates sum, average, count, minimum, and maximum for a selected field.

faq.question: Can it remove duplicates?
faq.answer: Yes. It removes duplicate records by tracking values from one selected field.

faq.question: Should I use it with sensitive data?
faq.answer: Use summaries when possible, and avoid sending full sensitive datasets back to the model.
